title: Relative Cech complexes agree for tuple and iterated 2-fibre-product presentations
statement:
Fix the universe and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention], a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], and a morphism $f:\mathcal U\to\mathcal X$ of categories fibred in groupoids over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Use their big etale sites (covering arrows lie over jointly surjective etale families) and abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $F$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal X$. For a functor $v:\mathcal V\to\mathcal X$ put $v^{-1}F=F\circ v$ contravariantly, and define $(v_*N)(x)=\Gamma(\mathcal V\times_{\mathcal X}T,N)$ for $x$ over $T$; restriction of $N$ to this 2-fibre product is understood, and $\Gamma$ means compatible families over all its objects.

For $p\geq0$ define $A_p(f)$ to have objects $(u_0,\ldots,u_p,y,\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_p)$ over the same scheme, with isomorphisms $\alpha_i:f(u_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}y$. An arrow to $(u'_0,\ldots,u'_p,y',\alpha'_0,\ldots,\alpha'_p)$ consists of arrows $b_i:u_i\to u'_i$ and $c:y\to y'$ over the same base arrow satisfying $c\alpha_i=\alpha'_if(b_i)$. Let $a_p:A_p(f)\to\mathcal X$ send this object to $y$. Put $A_{-1}(f)=\mathcal X$. The faces delete the indicated $u_i,\alpha_i$, with $A_0(f)\to A_{-1}(f)$ equal to $a_0$. Set $\widetilde E^{-1}(f,F)=F$, $\widetilde E^p(f,F)=(a_p)_*a_p^{-1}F$ for $p\geq0$, with zero terms below $-1$, augmentation restriction, and differential $\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^jd_j^*$ in degree $p\geq0$.

Let $\mathcal U_p$ instead be any iterated $(p+1)$-fold 2-fibre-product presentation of the Cech nerve of $f$, including $\mathcal U_0=\mathcal U$, with its usual compatible omission maps and map $f_p:\mathcal U_p\to\mathcal X$. Put $E^{-1}=F$ and $E^p=(f_p)_*f_p^{-1}F$, with the same augmentation and alternating differential. The equivalences between these 2-fibre-product presentations induce an isomorphism of augmented complexes of abelian sheaves
$$\Phi_F:E^\bullet(f,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde E^\bullet(f,F).$$
It is the identity in degree $-1$, commutes with augmentation and every coface map, and is natural in $F$. In particular the common-target tuple presentation, despite its redundant degree-zero category, computes the original augmented relative Cech complex without any covering or faithfulness hypothesis on $f$.

proof.text: Fix $x\in\mathcal X(T)$ and $p\geq0$. For each $t:R\to T$ choose a cartesian lift $x_t\to x$, with the identity choice for $t=1_T$. The unique factorization property in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] makes these a functor $h_T\to\mathcal X$: for $h:R\to R'$ over $T$ the arrow $x_t\to x_{t'}$ is the unique arrow whose composite to $x$ is the chosen one; uniqueness proves identity and composition. Work in the small models of [def-weil-size-convention]. Define $C_p(x)$ to have objects $(t:R\to T,u_0,\ldots,u_p,\gamma_i:f(u_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}x_t)$ and arrows $(h,b_i)$ satisfying $x(h)\gamma_i=\gamma_i'f(b_i)$. Let $D_x:C_p(x)^{op}\to\mathrm{Ab}$ have value $F(x_t)$ and restriction $F(x(h))$. Write $L_p(x,F)$ for its compatible families. Such families, with componentwise addition, are a limit: a map to the family group is uniquely determined by its component maps and these land in the family group precisely when they form a cone. No existence of a limit over a larger index category is being assumed.

source.place: 06X3 (section-cech), common-target objects; equation-pushforward preceding 06X7; small-skeleton implementation

proof.text: Put $V_A=A_p(f)\times_{\mathcal X}h_T$. Its objects are $(t,(u_i,y,\alpha_i),\beta:y\xrightarrow{\sim}x_t)$. There is a functor $q_A:V_A\to C_p(x)$ sending these data to $(t,u_i,\beta\alpha_i)$ and an inverse-on-one-side $j_A$ sending $(t,u_i,\gamma_i)$ to $(t,(u_i,x_t,\gamma_i),1_{x_t})$. They satisfy $q_Aj_A=1$. The arrows with leaf components $1_{u_i}$ and target component $\beta$ give $1_{V_A}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_Aq_A$; the arrow equations and naturality are exactly $\beta\alpha_i=\gamma_i$. The coefficient at an object of $V_A$ is $F(y)$; $F(\beta):F(x_t)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(y)$ is a natural coefficient isomorphism. Thus both the equivalence and its coefficient comparison are explicit, including when $p=0$.

Describe a bracketed iterated product by its binary tree $B$. At a leaf $i$ its value is $u_i$, its root object is $r_i=f(u_i)$, and its root comparison is $\lambda_i=1$. At a vertex $B=(B_L,B_R)$ an object is $(z_L,z_R,\theta:r_L\xrightarrow{\sim}r_R)$; choose $r_B=r_R$. Set $\lambda_i^B=\theta\lambda_i^{B_L}$ on the left leaves and $\lambda_i^B=\lambda_i^{B_R}$ on the right leaves. An arrow is a pair of subtree arrows with root arrows $c_L,c_R$ obeying $c_R\theta=\theta'c_L$. Substituting the displayed formulas gives $c_R\lambda_i^B=\lambda_i^{B\prime}f(b_i)$ for every leaf, by induction from the identity at a leaf. This constructs the flattening functor on all objects and arrows without discarding any automorphisms. For $V_B=B\times_{\mathcal X}h_T$ define $q_B:V_B\to C_p(x)$ by $\gamma_i=\beta\lambda_i^B$, where $\beta:r_B\xrightarrow{\sim}x_t$. Its coefficient comparison is $F(\beta):F(x_t)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(r_B)$.

source.place: 06X3 (section-cech), made explicit using Categories 0040 (lemma-2-product-categories-over-C), recursive object-and-isomorphism model

proof.text: Here is the inverse recursion, which also proves the required equivalence. Given $(t,u_i,\gamma_i)$, at a leaf set $z_i=u_i$ and $\beta_i=\gamma_i$. Having reconstructed the two subtrees and maps $\beta_L:r_L\to x_t$, $\beta_R:r_R\to x_t$, put $\theta=\beta_R^{-1}\beta_L$ and $\beta_B=\beta_R$. Then $\beta_B\theta\lambda_i^L=\beta_L\lambda_i^L=\gamma_i$ on the left and $\beta_B\lambda_i^R=\gamma_i$ on the right. This gives $j_B$ with $q_Bj_B=1$. Conversely, from any $(z,\beta)$, the recursion recovers its internal comparisons since $(\beta_R)^{-1}\beta_L=\theta$; hence $j_Bq_B=1$ in this explicit model. For arrows the same induction applies: the leaf compatibility gives $x(h)\beta_i=\beta_i'f(b_i)$, and at each vertex it gives $c_R\theta=\theta'c_L$ by cancellation of $\beta_R'$. Thus the inverse is a functor and the assertions include arrows over nonidentity base maps.

source.place: 06X3 (section-cech); Categories 0040 (lemma-2-product-categories-over-C), explicit inverse to the recursive normalization

proof.text: The preceding coordinates work for every bracketing. Choosing the other projection at a vertex changes its root by the specified invertible arrow $\theta$ and changes the coefficient by $F(\theta)$, so gives the same comparison after that identification. For any other representative of a binary $2$-fibre product, its defining cone property gives functors each way respecting the two projections and their comparison: a functor into that product is a pair of functors together with an invertible comparison, and a transformation is a pair satisfying its square. Applying this description to the identity pair in both directions shows that the composites are isomorphic to the identities by the unique projection-compatible transformations. Iterating at the vertices therefore gives the equivalence with the explicit tree model, with its root comparison. For omission maps, both resulting functors have the same retained leaf projections and comparisons; the same description gives their unique compatible $2$-isomorphism. This justifies arbitrary representatives as well as bracketings, and records the compatibility rather than requiring strict equality of nerve functors.

source.place: 06X3 (section-cech), meaning of a presentation; Categories 0040 (lemma-2-product-categories-over-C), cone description and uniqueness

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-limit] to the opposites of $j_A$ and $j_B$ (composed with the representative equivalence if necessary). To check its hypotheses for an equivalence $H:I\to J$, choose a quasi-inverse and counit. In the category of pairs $(i,a:H(i)\to y)$ the pair $(H^{-1}y,\epsilon_y)$ is terminal: full faithfulness lifts $\epsilon_y^{-1}a$ uniquely. This supplies nonemptiness and the required zigzags; a cospan $i\to k\leftarrow i'$ is written in that node's alternating convention as $i\leftarrow i\to k\leftarrow i'\to i'$, padding by identities. Thus restriction on compatible families is an isomorphism. Use also the coefficient isomorphisms $F(\beta)$ from steps 2 and 3, component by component (their inverses are $F(\beta^{-1})$). This gives additive isomorphisms $R_A:\widetilde E^p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_p(x,F)$ and $R_B:E^p(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_p(x,F)$. Set $\Phi^p(x)=R_A^{-1}R_B$. A natural coefficient isomorphism sends compatible families to compatible families because its square holds on each arrow; its inverse does the same, so no separate coefficient-transport theorem is needed.

source.place: 06X5 (lemma-generalities), proof of (2), and 06X9 (lemma-generalities-sheafified), equivalence invariance on sections

proof.text: These isomorphisms commute with restrictions in $x$. Indeed, for $a:x'\to x$ over $t:T'\to T$, the lift $x'_{t'}\to x'$ composed with $a$ factors uniquely through $x_{tt'}\to x$ by a vertical isomorphism $k:x'_{t'}\xrightarrow{\sim}x_{tt'}$. Both ways of restricting a component use $F(k)$ and replace each $\gamma_i$ by $k\gamma_i$. Equality follows from the family compatibility equations. For two composable arrows the two factorizations coincide by cartesianness, so these equalities respect composition. The same argument compares any two choices of cartesian lifts. Hence $\Phi^p$ is a natural transformation of presheaves with a natural inverse. The terms are abelian sheaves. Indeed $f_p$ and $a_p$ are functors over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ of categories fibred in groupoids, so they preserve cartesian arrows and [lem-sfb-fibred-site-functor-continuity] makes them continuous and cocontinuous for the big etale topologies. By [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-topos-adjunction], precomposition and the family functor $R$ indexed by pairs $(a,\psi:v(a)\to x)$ send sheaves of sets to sheaves of sets. Sending $(t,a,\phi:v(a)\xrightarrow{\sim}x_t)$ to $(a,(x_t\to x)\circ\phi)$ is an isomorphism of index categories, inverse to the unique cartesian factorization, compatibly with restrictions; so $(v_*N)(x)=RN(x)$ on underlying sets, and an abelian presheaf whose underlying presheaf of sets is a sheaf is an abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. These natural transformations are therefore morphisms of abelian sheaves, since [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] defines that category as a full subcategory of presheaves.

source.place: 06X9 (lemma-generalities-sheafified), evaluated on objects as in 06XB (remark-cech-complex-sections); sheaf property of the pushforward terms as in 06X7 (section-sheaf-cech-complex) and equation-pushforward

proof.text: Check every face before taking alternating sums. In $C_{p+1}(x)$ the face $d_j$ simply forgets $(u_j,\gamma_j)$. In tuple coordinates this is exactly deletion. In tree coordinates every internal comparison reconstructed from the retained leaves is $\beta_R^{-1}\beta_L$ as in step 4. If the distinguished root leaf is deleted, the new root comparison is the retained $\gamma_i$, and the old-to-new root comparison is $\gamma_i^{-1}\beta$; composing with $\gamma_i$ recovers $\beta$. Thus the coefficient maps also agree: contravariance gives $F(\gamma_i^{-1}\beta)F(\gamma_i)=F(\beta)$. These equations say precisely that restricting a family before or after a face gives the same component; step 5 supplies the projection-compatible comparison for other representatives. Therefore $R_A$ and $R_B$ identify every coface with pullback under the same deletion functor, and $\Phi^{p+1}d_j^*=d_j^*\Phi^p$. Summing with coefficients $(-1)^j$ proves compatibility with the differentials.

Set $\Phi^{-1}=1_F$ and use the unique maps between zero objects in lower degrees. On an object $(t,u_0,\gamma_0)$ of $C_0(x)$, augmentation sends $s\in F(x)$ to its restriction $F(x_t\to x)(s)\in F(x_t)$. Both models give exactly this value: their further coefficient comparison is the already specified $F(\beta)$. Hence $\Phi^0$ commutes with augmentation. For a morphism $\eta:F\to G$, every component of $R_A$ and $R_B$ commutes with $\eta$, since $\eta$ commutes with all the restriction maps $F(\beta)$ and with the maps defining compatible families. The inverses also commute, by composing with these isomorphisms. Consequently $\Phi$ is natural in $F$ and is an isomorphism of augmented complexes. The construction has used only invertible comparison arrows, cartesian factorization and restriction of compatible families, so has required neither a cover nor faithfulness of $f$.
